stories.head: Russian strike on flats near Kyiv leaves at least two dead and many missing
stories.say: A Russian strike tore through a five-storey block of flats in Dymer, north of Kyiv, on Sunday. Two bodies have been recovered and children are among the missing.
stories.stand: Part of a five-storey building collapsed in Dymer, as Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the US to release Patriot interceptors that allies have paid for.
body: A Russian strike destroyed part of a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, on Sunday, Ukrainian officials said. Kyiv regional military administration head Timur Tkachenko said two bodies had been recovered and at least four people were injured.

Ukrainian police listed 15 people as missing, including two children. Interfax, cited by Al Jazeera, put the number of missing at 11. In Zaporizhzhia, a man was killed in Russian shelling, the regional administration said.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia had fired about 2,700 attack drones, 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine in a week. He urged the US to approve deliveries of Patriot interceptors that partners have already paid for.

stories.head: Russian navy ship hit by suspected sea drones at Libyan port
stories.say: A Russian navy ship docked at Benghazi in eastern Libya was hit by a suspected sea drone on Sunday, causing an explosion and a fire. Libya and Russia will investigate.
stories.stand: Eastern Libya's government called it a violation of sovereignty and said it would investigate with Russia; no one has claimed the attack.
body: A Russian vessel docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya was hit by a suspected sea drone on Sunday, causing an explosion and a brief fire, the eastern government said. It said the fire was brought under control.
Two Libyan military officials, speaking anonymously to the Associated Press via ITV, named the ship as the corvette Merkury. They said at least four drones were intercepted and two hit the ship.

The eastern government said Libya is not a party to the war between Russia and Ukraine. It announced a joint investigation with Russia into the source of the attack. Neither Russia nor Ukraine commented immediately, and no group claimed responsibility.

stories.head: Iran's navy says it set two tankers ablaze near the Strait of Hormuz
stories.say: Iranian media say two oil tankers caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, after Iran's navy said they had entered a restricted area and broken its rules.
stories.stand: Iran's navy said the ships entered a restricted area east of the strait; a Revolutionary Guards commander warned of attempts to stir unrest.
body: Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, according to Iranian media. Iran's navy said the ships had entered a restricted area east of the strait and were set ablaze for breaking its rules.
The deputy commander of the Revolutionary Guards, Major-General Mostafa Izadi, said Iran's enemies were seeking instability by increasing economic pressure, the state news agency IRNA reported.
Separately, a ship-tracking site said an Iranian tanker reported to be sailing through the strait did not exist, Euronews reported. The ships' owners and the extent of damage have not been confirmed.

stories.head: Poland says Russia tried twice to kill Ukrainian-US rapper Kyivstoner
stories.say: Poland says Russian intelligence twice tried to kill the Ukrainian-American rapper known as Kyivstoner, first in Poland in August and then at a concert near Copenhagen.
stories.stand: Poland's foreign ministry said a Danish plot was the second attempt on the same man; Russia calls the allegations unsubstantiated.
body: Poland says Russian intelligence tried twice to kill Albert Vasiliev, a Ukrainian-American rapper who performs as Kyivstoner. Polish authorities detained a Russian national on 7 August after foiling a plot in Poland, the foreign ministry said.

Denmark expelled a Russian diplomat on Friday over an alleged plot at a September concert near Copenhagen. Two Danish men face charges of assisting a foreign intelligence service and attempted murder.
Poland's foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewior confirmed on Sunday that Warsaw regards it as the second attempt on the same person. Russia says the allegations are unsubstantiated.

stories.head: 24 body bags recovered after fire at Indonesian sweet factory
stories.say: Police in Indonesia have recovered twenty-four body bags from a sweet factory in Banten province that caught fire on Saturday, and twenty-nine workers are still missing.
stories.stand: The fire broke out at a confectionery plant in Serang regency, on Java; the search for missing workers resumes on Monday.
body: A fire broke out on Saturday evening at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia sweet factory in Cikande, Serang regency, on Indonesia's island of Java. Police have removed 24 body bags from the site, Al Jazeera reported.

According to the factory, 29 of the 65 workers believed to be in the affected area are missing, four are being treated and eight are unaccounted for. Banten police chief Hendra Kurniawan said the search was paused overnight and would resume on Monday.
Police said DNA identification could take two to three weeks. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

stories.head: Drone attacks kill four near Khartoum and damage a UN building
stories.say: Drone attacks in and around Khartoum killed four people early on Sunday, including a child, and damaged a UN building while staff were inside.
stories.stand: Local reports and UN officials blamed the Rapid Support Forces for the overnight strikes in Sudan.
body: Drone attacks between about 2am and 4.30am on Sunday killed four people in and around Khartoum, Al Jazeera reported. Local reports and UN officials blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
Three people were killed and nine wounded when a drone hit a home in northern Omdurman. A child died in a separate strike south of the capital.
The UN humanitarian coordinator for Sudan, Denise Brown, said a UN building was damaged while staff were inside.

stories.head: WHO says fighting near an Ebola hospital in DR Congo puts workers at risk
stories.say: The World Health Organization's chief says heavy fighting near a hospital in Congo's Ituri province trapped health workers for more than a day, disrupting the Ebola response.
stories.stand: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for peace as the outbreak passed 11,000 cases, according to WHO figures.
body: Heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, disrupted Ebola response work, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Sunday. Health workers and aid partners sheltered in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.
He said patients, families and health workers faced grave risk and that the WHO was working to arrange their safe exit.
As of 17 November, the WHO had recorded 11,613 cases and 5,678 deaths in the outbreak. Ituri and North Kivu are the hardest-hit provinces.

stories.head: Likud and Eisenkot's Yashar end coalition talks without a deal
stories.say: Coalition talks in Israel between Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar ended on Sunday without a deal, split over who leads first and Itamar Ben-Gvir's role.
stories.stand: Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government; his bloc holds 48 seats, 13 short of a majority.
body: Unity talks between Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party ended on Sunday without agreement, Al Jazeera reported. The parties remain split over who would serve first as prime minister and whether far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would join.
Both sides plan to meet again, but no date has been set. Eisenkot must form a government by 6 December, a deadline that can be extended by 14 days.
His bloc holds 48 seats, 13 short of a majority. If talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote for a minority government backed by Arab parties, according to the report.

stories.head: Belgian airports shut for Monday's national strike against cuts
stories.say: Almost all flights in and out of Belgium are expected to be cancelled on Monday, as air traffic control stops work during a national strike against government spending cuts.
stories.stand: Air traffic controller Skeyes suspends services from 7am to 9pm as unions rally in Brussels against austerity.
body: Belgian air traffic controller Skeyes is suspending services from 7am to 9pm on Monday, so nearly all flights are expected to be cancelled, Al Jazeera reported. All Belgian airports are affected, including Brussels and Brussels-Charleroi.
The shutdown is part of a national strike by unions against government austerity. A large rally is planned in Brussels, and transport, schools and offices may also be disrupted.
Prime Minister Bart De Wever is negotiating cuts worth 10 billion euros with coalition partners to reduce the deficit. Airline representatives say it is the 11th airspace strike in 11 months.

stories.head: Mongolia's president resigns, triggering a snap election
stories.say: Mongolia's parliament has accepted the resignation of President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa, the first time a sitting president has quit early. He denies corruption claims against him.
stories.stand: Parliament voted 96 of 104 in favour of accepting the resignation; the speaker becomes acting president.
body: Mongolia's parliament accepted the resignation of President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa on Thursday, with 96 of 104 members voting in favour, Euronews reported. It is the first time a sitting president has resigned before the end of a term.
He denies corruption claims made by former justice minister Nyambaatar Khishgee, who alleges he received money linked to a railway project when he was prime minister.
Speaker Sandag Byambatsogt becomes acting president. Inflation in Mongolia has reached 13.6%, its highest since 2022.

stories.head: Brazil's Jair Bolsonaro in intensive care with intestinal blockage
stories.say: Brazil's former president Jair Bolsonaro is in intensive care in Brasília with an intestinal obstruction. The hospital says he is stable, conscious and breathing unaided.
stories.stand: Bolsonaro, serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup under humanitarian house arrest, was taken to hospital on Saturday.
body: Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro was admitted to intensive care on Saturday with an intestinal obstruction, Euronews reported. Military police escorted him to DF Star Hospital in Brasília.
The hospital said he was clinically stable, conscious, alert and breathing without assistance. Doctors inserted a gastric tube and have not ruled out further surgery.
Bolsonaro was convicted of plotting a coup, which he denies. He is serving a sentence of 27 years and three months under humanitarian house arrest granted in March.

stories.stand: The Israeli military said police and investigators had been sent to collect evidence.
body: Israeli settlers attacked several Palestinian villages in the central occupied West Bank on Sunday, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. They burned 12 vehicles and spray-painted racist slogans on homes.
The villages named were Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan, in the Ramallah and al-Bireh area. No injuries were reported.
The Israeli military said police and investigators were sent to collect evidence.

stories.head: About 1,800 Met Police staff have left since 2022 over standards failures
stories.say: About eighteen hundred Metropolitan Police staff have left since 2022 over misconduct, vetting or performance failures, according to internal figures.
stories.stand: Internal reports of abuse and corruption nearly tripled to 1,348 in 2023-24, according to figures reported by the Press Association.
body: About 1,800 Metropolitan Police staff have left since 2022 over misconduct, performance, vetting or probation failures, or quit during standards investigations, according to internal figures reported by the Press Association and ITV News.
The share of recruits failing a stricter vetting process has doubled to more than 10%. Internal reports of abuse and corruption nearly tripled to 1,348 in 2023-24, the latest full year of data.
Deputy Commissioner Matt Jukes told The Observer he did not subscribe to the 'rotten apples' theory, and said the problems went beyond a few individuals.

stories.head: Two Afghan men convicted of sexual attack on girl, 14, on Kent train
stories.say: Two Afghan men have been convicted of sexually attacking a fourteen-year-old girl on a train in Kent. The Home Office says it will pursue deportation after sentencing.
stories.stand: Baryalai Rahimi and Mirebadurahman Sadat will be sentenced on 18 December.
body: Two Afghan men, Baryalai Rahimi, 25, and Mirebadurahman Sadat, 29, were convicted at Inner London Crown Court of attacking a 14-year-old girl on a London-bound train, ITV News reported. They had approached her at Sturry station near Canterbury on 5 February.

Rahimi was found guilty of rape, sexual assault and three counts of sexual activity with a child. Sadat was found guilty of assault by penetration, sexual activity with a child and two counts of causing a person to engage in sexual activity.
They will be sentenced on 18 December. The Home Office said it would pursue deportation after sentencing.

stories.stand: Brand is serving 10.5 years after being convicted of rape and sexual assault at Southwark Crown Court.
body: Laura Gallacher, the wife of Russell Brand, said she would honour the rules set by prison staff after reading a message from him on their YouTube podcast, ITV News reported. The message, in which he protested his innocence, prompted an investigation into possible breaches of prison rules.
The video remains on his channel despite requests from ministers. Google reportedly declined to remove it, saying its rules had not been broken.
Brand is serving a sentence of 10.5 years after his conviction on 5 November at Southwark Crown Court for one count of rape and three sexual assaults.

body: Independent Bradford councillor Ibrar Ali, 52, was stabbed while door-knocking at about 11am on Thursday, the Yorkshire Post reported.

Police said they had no information suggesting the attack was politically motivated.

stories.stand: Wes Streeting met Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday; most of a £260m drone order is expected to go to UK firms.
body: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting visited Kyiv on Saturday and met President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Defence Minister Khmara, the government said. New agreements allow Ukrainian-designed strike drones to be produced in the UK for Ukraine's armed forces.
The UK's £500 million package includes £240 million for more than 1,000 air-defence missiles, and £260 million for more than 1,000 long-range strike drones and other drones.
More than 80% of the drone money is expected to go to UK companies, the government said. The UK has committed £3 billion a year in military support.

stories.head: UK joins Nato project to launch military satellites quickly
stories.say: The UK has joined a Nato project called Starlift to build a network of commercially supplied satellite launches, with SaxaVord spaceport in Shetland as the key British site.
stories.stand: Ministers announced the move on Sunday alongside £30 million set aside for orbital launch readiness.
body: The UK has joined Nato's Starlift initiative with ten allies, aiming to build a network of flexible, commercially supplied satellite launch capabilities, the government said on Sunday.

It was announced by Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and space minister Baroness Lloyd. The project has four strands, covering launch contracts, rapid launch testing, infrastructure, and regulation and traffic management.
The main UK site is SaxaVord Spaceport in Shetland, approved for up to 30 launches a year. The government has earmarked £30 million for orbital launch readiness.

stories.say: Villagers in Barnham, Suffolk, have voted two hundred and fifty-seven to sixteen in a symbolic poll to leave the UK, in protest at plans to house asylum seekers at a nearby RAF base.
stories.stand: The vote has no legal weight; the government has not made a final decision on housing 931 men at RAF Barnham.
body: Residents of Barnham in Suffolk voted 257 to 16 in a symbolic poll on independence from the UK, ITV News reported. There was one spoilt ballot.
The vote was a protest against plans to house 931 male asylum seekers at RAF Barnham. The number was reduced from an initial figure of up to 1,256.
The poll has no legal weight, and the government's final decision is still pending.

stories.head: Crane begins lifting collapsed Pero's Bridge out of Bristol harbour
stories.say: A barge-mounted crane has begun lifting the collapsed Pero's Bridge out of Bristol's harbour. A council report found the footbridge had not been properly tested for almost a decade.
stories.stand: The footbridge collapsed on 31 October; no one was hurt, and its three spans are being moved to Albion Dry Dock.
body: Work to lift Pero's Bridge out of Bristol's Floating Harbour began on Sunday, when a barge-mounted crane was due to move its three spans to Albion Dry Dock over several days, ITV News reported.
The footbridge collapsed at 11pm on 31 October. No one was injured. An engineering assessment suggests external vibration was the most likely factor.
A council report found the bridge had not been properly tested for almost a decade because of the weight of padlocks attached to it.

stories.head: Democrats reach their biggest US House majority since 1992
stories.say: Democrats have won at least two hundred and fifty-eight House seats, their highest total since 1992, after a recount in North Carolina unseated the long-serving Republican Virginia Foxx.
stories.stand: Chuck Hubbard won North Carolina's 5th district by 330 votes after a recount, the Associated Press projected on Sunday.
body: Democrats have won at least 258 seats in the US House of Representatives, their highest total since 1992, Al Jazeera reported. The Associated Press called the final deciding race on Sunday after a recount.
In North Carolina's 5th congressional district, Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated the Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx, who had served 11 terms. The margin was 330 votes as of Sunday.
Four House races from the 3 November midterms remain uncalled. Democrats will also hold 56 Senate seats in the new Congress.

stories.head: Trump attacks Schumer ahead of Senate Democrats' leadership vote

stories.stand: Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats since 2017, says he will be elected; Chris Van Hollen also says he is confident.
body: President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sunday that it would be very hard to work with Chuck Schumer if he becomes Senate majority leader, Al Jazeera reported.

Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats since 2017, faces a challenge from Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen. A closed-door, secret-ballot vote is scheduled for 1 December. Both men say they are confident of winning.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll in mid-November found 34% of Democrats viewed Schumer favourably, down from 38% in February.

stories.head: Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin may hold an 11th-century abbot
stories.say: Researchers say the skeleton in a Roman stone coffin at Westminster Abbey may be the abbot Aelfwig, who died around 1020, ending a hundred-and-fifty-year mystery.
stories.stand: Radiocarbon dating places the burial in the late Saxon period, between 987 and 1052 AD.
body: The skeleton in Westminster Abbey's Roman sarcophagus, excavated in 1869, may be the medieval abbot Aelfwig, who died around 1020, researchers say, ScienceDaily reported. An alternative candidate is Wulnoth, who died in 1049.
Radiocarbon dating gave a range of 987 to 1052 AD, placing the burial in the late Saxon period. Bone analysis suggests a man aged 35 to 49.
Consultant archaeologist Warwick Rodwell published the findings in the Journal of the British Archaeological Association.

stories.head: Lock of George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
stories.say: A lock of George Washington's hair has sold for four thousand dollars at an auction in South Carolina. It came from the family of a hotelier who hosted his last two birthday celebrations.
stories.stand: The framed lock was sold by Richmond Auctions on Saturday.
body: A lock of George Washington's hair sold for $4,000 at Richmond Auctions in South Carolina on Saturday, CBS News reported.
The collector John K. Lattimer obtained it from the family of John Gadsby, an Alexandria, Virginia, hotelier who hosted Washington's final two birthday celebrations. The buyer was not named.

stories.head: Tom Jackson, Broncos linebacker turned ESPN analyst, dies at 75
stories.say: Tom Jackson, who played fourteen seasons for the Denver Broncos before thirty-two years as an ESPN analyst, has died at seventy-five, his family and ESPN said.
stories.stand: He appeared on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown alongside Chris Berman.
body: Tom Jackson, a former Denver Broncos linebacker and ESPN analyst, has died aged 75, his family and ESPN announced on Sunday, CBS News reported. His family said he died on Friday.

He played 14 seasons for the Broncos, from 1973 to 1986, and was part of their first Super Bowl team. He then spent 32 years at ESPN, appearing on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown with Chris Berman.

stories.stand: The Independent Public Media Board, which oversees the transition, made the appointment.

body: Inter Miami lost 3-0 at home to Columbus Crew on Saturday in the first game of their best-of-three MLS Cup play-off series, Al Jazeera reported.

Miami will be eliminated if Columbus win the next game in Ohio on Friday.
